links.comparator_used: Expert educator ratings of the cases (physiotherapy educators rated medical accuracy, realism, fidelity, relevance and usability), used as the reference for the automated DeepEval LLM-as-judge scores
links.outcome: Agreement between automated LLM-judge metrics and expert ratings of synthetic case quality
links.effect: Completeness metric vs expert usability ρ ≈ 0.393 (moderate); answer relevance and prompt alignment showed weak or negative correlations with clinical correctness. 90 of 128 cases (70.3%) passed automated screening.
links.tradeoff: The LLM judge missed subtle clinical reasoning failures (reductive logic, biomechanical inconsistency, administrative/contextual gaps), so expert review was still needed to protect clinical accuracy.
links.quote: Cross-layer correlation analysis revealed that automated completeness metrics moderately aligned with expert usability ratings (  ρ ≈ 0.393), while answer relevance and prompt alignment showed weak or negative correlations with clinical correctness.

design_hint: LLM-as-judge automated screening plus expert educator review of generated cases
